heofonan is accusative singular of supplied weak feminine heofone, not a plural of productive masculine heofon.

In ofer ðǣre nēowolnesse brādnesse, ofer governs dative brādnesse; ðǣre nēowolnesse is its genitive dependent.
ofer wæteru has accusative plural wæteru; supply the actual local government, without generalizing all ofer phrases.
wæs gefęred is the complete supplied passive 'was borne/carried', contextually 'moved'.
Geweorðe lēoht is supplied as 'Let light come to be'; finite third singular present subjunctive/optative, not infinitive or indicative.
wearð geworht is the complete supplied passive 'was made/came into being'.
ðæt hit gōd wæs means 'that it was good'; ðæt is a conjunction, hit refers to light, and wæs follows the predicate in this embedded clause.
Supply hē 'he' referring to God and hit 'it' referring to neuter light; do not infer a productive pronoun paradigm.
Supply temporal ðā 'then', distinct from the identically spelled accusative/nominative plural or feminine accusative article.
hēt takes object and naming accusatives; God/hē is the understood subject. Supply the complete naming frame.

Supply the complete first-day formula Ðā wæs geworden ǣfen and morgen ān dæg. Its resultative/perfect phrase is distinct from the earlier passives; do not demand unique subject/predicate analysis or generalize agreement from it.
Use a dative recipient and accusative thing given in the explicitly supplied sealde frame; distinguish to/for-recipient from the direct object.
Complete selected personal N/D/A and third-person G forms; singular, dual, plural and third-person singular gender.
Recognize first/second-person genitive person/number; inflecting attributive possessives wait for Unit3.
Dual subjects take ordinary plural verb forms; object pronouns do not control finite agreement.
Use nominative subjects and governed object/recipient cases; grammatical gender/number tracks referents, including inanimate nouns. Syncretic spelling alone does not settle antecedence.
his/hiere/hiera are invariant possessors; possessor reference determines choice, while the head keeps its own case/number.
Complete present/preterite indicative morphology of22 affirmative weak lemma systems; class/stem changes are not inferred from infinitive ending alone.
Long-stem ClassI full indicative; all assigned dental/consonant subpatterns together with exact2/3singular and preterite surfaces.
sęllan and gewyrcean: explicitly learned irregular preterite stems; no unrestricted prefix rule.
Short/geminated gefręmman and sonorant ęfnan: full finite paradigms, geminate/simple alternation and linking vowel.
Short ClassI nęrian full finite paradigm, distinguished from ClassII -ian.
Full ClassII lufian/geblētsian/gehālgian present/preterite, selected -ode/-odon series.
Complete selected present/preterite of habban; source alternatives separate.
Complete selected present/preterite of libban; source alternatives separate.
Complete selected present/preterite of secgan; source alternatives separate.
Complete selected present/preterite of hycgan; source alternatives separate.
Recognize full contracted negative companion of habban; no unaided production required.
Identify finite preterites using supplied principal-part entries; no infinitive, passive, perfect or participial syntax follows from citation display.
Ordinary independent active clauses: nominative subject, finite person/number agreement. Exercise order is a model, not a universal mandatory rule.

Accusative object with audited senses of hīeran, cyssan, sęttan, sęndan, lǣdan, mētan, nęrian, lufian, habban, gefyllan, gewyrcean, gefręmman, geblētsian, gehālgian and the thing given with sęllan. Not every weak verb governs accusative.
Independently formed sęllan: dative recipient, accusative thing, noun/pronoun arguments. No sęndan recipient government inferred.
Personal pronouns reflexively: geręstan+accusative self and sęllan with dative recipient coreferential with subject. No self adjective.
Coordinate simple clauses/predicates with and, allowing the same subject to remain understood in the second finite predicate of the stated examples.

ne before noncontracting finite weak verbs in simple clauses. nabban is recognition-only; uncontracted ne hæbbe is source-permitted and valid contractions remain valid. Negative copula/concord not assigned.
Subject+sęcgan introduces a direct independent utterance with colon/quotation marks. Quoted pronouns belong to its speaker; no indirect complement syntax.
Intransitive live with prior locative on+dative; no new object or goal government.
wǣron fullfręmede = were completed/finished; the coordinated subject is the heavens, the earth, and all their array. wǣron is a familiar form but this use with a participle remains supplied.
Eornostlice = accordingly/thus; ðā = then, an adverb rather than the identically spelled article. No article form is being parsed at those tokens.
eall hiera frætwung = all their array; eall modifies feminine singular frætwung. fram eallum ðǣm weorce = from all the work; eallum and ðǣm agree with neuter dative singular weorce.
ðone seofoðan dæg = the seventh day: masculine accusative singular with the actual weak ordinal form seofoðan. No other ordinal forms are required.

on ðone seofoðan dæg = on the seventh day; on ðone dæg = on that day/the day just named. These are temporal phrases with accusative. Do not replace dæg with dative dæge or infer motion. Unit 1 locative on + dative does not license this use.

ðe introduces which/that clauses referring to work: which he made; which he performed; which he created to make. The relative particle represents the direct object within each clause, although its antecedents weorc, weorce, weorces have different external cases. Supply clause boundaries and this relation; do not assign general relative syntax.

Here geręstan + reflexive pronoun + fram-phrase means rest from work. fram governs dative weorce. The form of fram and separation use were taught in Unit 1, but that contract confined independent use to a supplied separating frame.
for-ðon-ðe introduces the reason: because he ceased from his work on that day. The clause continues through the final supplied relative/infinitive phrase.

geswāc his weorces = ceased from his work. geswāc governs genitive weorces; his is its possessive genitive, not a second direct object. The known genitive form does not imply this new government was taught.

ðe hē gescēop tō wyrceanne = which he created to make. Cook gives Latin creavit ut faceret and the margin rendering created to make. tō wyrceanne is an inflected infinitive indicating the making for which he created the work. Preserve the actual source relation; do not silently substitute created and made or finished creating. This compact calque is supplied whole, with no independent infinitive target or unique idiomatic-translation demand.
Adjectives agree with their own noun/referent in case, number and gender; attributive and ordinary positive predicate uses are taught.
Complete selected strong N/G/D/A singular/plural in all genders; lexical alternations and distinct reference instrumentals are identified.
Complete selected weak N/G/D/A singular/plural; ordinary genitive plural -ra and explicitly audited comparative exceptions.
Long adjective stems: zero feminine nominative singular and neuter N/A plural in selected monosyllabic strong paradigms.
Short adjective stems: selected -u in feminine nominative singular and neuter N/A plural; complete lexical paradigms determine spelling.
glæd alternates æ/a in its checked cells; this is not an unrestricted substitution rule.
Selected disyllabic stems and vowel loss are taught together with exceptions; preserve the audited cell rather than delete every medial vowel.
Complete -e adjective pattern represented by æppelbǣre, distinguishing lexical -e from case endings.
Complete gearu pattern with checked u/w alternation.
Complete hēah pattern, including h loss and the selected contraction before endings.

Ordinary attributive adjectives are weak after article/demonstrative; bare ordinary adjectives are strong. After possessives Cook permits strong and sometimes weak; no universal possessive→weak rule and no new rule for adjectives after limiting genitives.
Ordinary positive predicative adjectives are strong and nominative, agreeing with the subject even when its noun phrase contains an article. Comparatives remain weak.
Recognize distinct masculine/neuter singular strong adjective and demonstrative instrumental citations; no instrumental construction is independently taught.
The six agreeing possessives have complete strong morphology. Their endings agree with the possessed noun, not the possessor; personal-genitive citations retain separate records.
Choose mīn/ðīn/uncer/incer/ūre/ēower for the possessor person/number, then inflect for the possessed head. Contrast prior invariant his/hiere/hiera. No self or sīn teaching.
Regular lēof/lēofra/lēofost series, with full assigned degree inflections.
eald/ieldra/ieldest is the assigned umlaut series; no universal umlaut instruction.
Complete selected gōd, yfel, micel and lȳtel comparison series; exact stems and superlative choices are lexical.
Comparatives are weak attributively and predicatively; full paradigms include transparently derived genitive plural contractions and licensed -ena selections.
Full strong/weak superlative morphology; ordinary attributive superlatives normally weak, taught predicate use strong. Partitive/substantival uses remain unassigned.
Bounded subject A + copula + comparative + ðonne + parallel subject B: B is nominative, with repeated copula understood. No generalized comparative-clause or genitive-standard syntax.
Selected supplied adjective citations wīd/swīð/sōð yield checked -e/-lice adverbs; no full adjective system implied by these citation bases.
Selected adverbs qualify actions or whole statements without case/number/gender agreement; sōðlice truly is distinct from the supplied source connective sense.
swīðe very qualifies an adjective; adverb has no adjective-agreement ending.
wīde/wīdor/wīdost and wel/bęt/bętst are invariant adverbial degrees; no new comparative-clause syntax.
Complete ān singular cardinal forms with singular count nouns; plural reference cells confer no productive plural-one sense.
Complete twēgen/ðrīe N/G/D/A plural across genders; no noun dual paradigm.
Checked cardinal 4–12 forms used invariantly before plural count nouns; no postposed/substantival inflection or higher-number partitive syntax.
Cardinal one with singular nouns, 2–12 with plural count nouns; numeral gender/case agrees where the selected system inflects.
Complete selected first, third–seventh weak paradigms express order. Ordinary noun case is supplied by already taught syntax; no temporal on+accusative production implied.
ōðer second remains strong even after the article; selected syncope and feminine ōðru with valid variants are explicit.
Complete ðes/ðēos/ðis system: this/these, agreeing with the noun in N/G/D/A; reference instrumentals do not create syntax milestones.
Existing se/sēo/ðæt morphology now also expresses pointing that/those; relative and general third-person pronoun uses remain unassigned.
Complete new ðing heavy-neuter paradigm in the sense thing/things; prior ordinary case constructions apply.
Counted lēoht luminary distinct from mass light; prior singular morphology retained and all four plural cases promoted to production.
Direct speech introduced by supplied cwæð, with then and connective sōðlice. Unit2 productive quotation was specifically with sęcgan.
Plural finite optatives express a wish/command. Bēon is not an infinitive; all coordinated verbs share the lights as subject.
on governs dative fæstnesse; ðǣre heofonan is embedded genitive feminine singular, from weak heofone.
tō + dative expresses assigned function/purpose. Noun cells are prior; this prepositional use is not taught by Unit2 tō wyrceanne.
Resultative fulfillment formula; prior wæs form does not establish independent perfect/resultative syntax.
gesętte has omitted God/he subject; hīe is accusative plural object. on ðǣre heofonan has dative feminine singular heofonan, not genitive.
ðæt introduces purpose; scinen, gīemden, tōdǣlden are past optatives. This is not the content-that sense.
ofer eorðan means over the earth. Source spelling eorðan is compatible with accusative or dative singular; do not require one uniquely.
gīeman governs genitive in this exact construction, explicitly documented by §156f. Genitive forms themselves are prior.
Supplied strong geseah plus content clause ðæt hit gōd wæs. New predicate-adjective morphology can be observed within supplied content-clause syntax.
Closing resultative formula and source word order supplied. The new ordinal fēorða agrees with dæg; męrgen is a source vowel variant of selected morgen.
Identify the four principal-part positions and distinguish finite preterite entries from supplied infinitive/participle citations.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: No unaided nonfinite recall, infinitive complement, participial agreement, perfect or passive syntax.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Distinguish strong preterite ablaut from the previously taught weak dental preterite.
Complete selected present and preterite indicative: all three persons, singular and plural; these tables introduce no other mood or nonfinite construction.
Present 1sg -e, 2sg -st and 3sg -ð with each audited stem/consonant adjustment; ordinary plural -að and the selected contracted plurals.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Postposed-pronoun plural -e is outside assigned learner scope, not a free alternative.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Past 1/3sg normally use the singular stem; 2sg uses the plural stem with -e and all plural persons use -on; findan has its separately taught selected exception.
Selected Class I ī : ā : i : i principal-part pattern, present stem and exact finite paradigms.
Selected Class II ēo/ū : ēa : u : o pattern, including its exact lexical singular present mutation.
Selected nasal Class III i : a : u : u finite systems (bindan, winnan, findan, drincan, singan), retaining lexical exceptions.
Helpan e/ea/u and gieldan ie/ea/u finite families with their distinct present singulars; selected vowels are short.
Weorpan and weorðan eo/ea/u finite family and separately audited forweorðan; present singular mutation remains lexical.
Berstan and separately audited tōberstan use e/æ/u with the selected metathesized order and present bierst.
The selected II and III second/third singular present vowels differ from present1/pl; exact lexical diagnostics, not an unrestricted replacement rule.
Audited dental/sibilant contractions, ð-stem effects, geminate reduction and bounded g/h variants in selected present2/3sg.
Lexical consonant alternation: snīðan/sēoðan/weorðan ð/d; cēosan s/r; contracted stems h/g, at their explicitly mapped positions.
Complete wrēon indicative with wrēo/wrīhst/wrīhð/wrēoð and wrāh/wrige/wrigon; no merger with the Class II homographic series.
Complete Class II tēon draw/pull indicative, with its selected contracted present and tēah/tuge/tugon past.
Select fand as past1sg, funde as past2sg and usual past3sg, fundon for all plural persons; admit first-person funde and third-person fand as documented alternatives.
Recognize complete bregdan and composite fēolan indicative references using displayed tables and their declared source/variant limits.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: No independent production or unassigned clause government; Cook folen remains the citation target.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Tōberstan and forweorðan are separately learned whole lexemes with full berstan/weorðan finite morphology.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: No productive prefix-attachment or automatic compositional-meaning rule.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Complete scip, wind, strand and gefēra NGDA singular/plural, using the prior complete noun patterns and independently checked lexical stems.
Selected ordinary transitive uses: drīfan drives cattle, bindan binds an animal, cēosan chooses a thing, findan finds a thing and drincan drinks water; the direct object is accusative.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Exact lexical government is independently evidenced. Cattle, an animal, ships and dwellings in these new compositions are declared ordinary lexical applications, not falsely attributed source quotations. No universal strong-verb accusative rule.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Rīdan ride and singan sing may stand without a nominal object; prior manner adverbs qualify the action.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: No directional complement or instrumental transport is implied by riding.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Helpan takes the dative being or recipient helped in the selected ordinary use. The attested person examples support the declared new application to birds.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Dative being/recipient is the selected target. Attested human examples support the explicitly declared ordinary lexical application to birds. The documented genitive alternative is valid but is not the construction requested here.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Ordinary weorðan become takes a nominative predicate adjective agreeing with its subject.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: New sense weorthan-become only; supplied passive weorthan-1 is not promoted.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Prior preverbal ne extends explicitly to the selected noncontracting strong indicatives.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: No negative copula, nillan, other contracted systems or negative concord is introduced.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Use the assigned strong preterites for successive past events in independent coordinated clauses, retaining prior subject agreement and direct quotation.
The ship breaks up with tōberstan and the companions perish with forweorðan; each is an intransitive subject–verb clause.
Ðǣr-tō-ēacan means in addition to that/besides: further winds join the already described storm. The preceding storm is summarized in separate English editorial context.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Fixed connective supplied; no productive compound-adverb rule.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: him ongēan stōd = stood against/opposed them. ongēan follows its dative pronoun. The natural local reading takes him as the preceding northeast winds, but its spelling also permits masculine/neuter singular and the antecedent is an editorial inference, not morphologically unique.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Do not demand unique number/antecedent identification from him alone; do not teach general postposition syntax. A justified alternative antecedent is not rejected solely for differing from the guiding inference.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: ðæt scip eall = the whole ship/all the ship. eall is strong neuter nominative singular, postposed to the subject noun phrase; its morphology/sense were recognition-only in Unit3.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Keep eall morphology and sense at their prior recognition milestone; the postposed whole/all construction is supplied, not independent production.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: on ðisse ęgeslican hrēohnesse = in this terrible tempest/storm. The noun phrase is feminine dative singular; ęgeslican is weak after the demonstrative. This abstract surrounding circumstance is supplied locally.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Prior spatial on+dative does not automatically establish every figurative/circumstantial sense.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Apollonius gefēran = Apollonius’s companions. Cook note1 explicitly identifies the foreign proper name here as genitive despite its -us appearance. gefēran is nominative plural, not a subject named Apollonius.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: The relation and before-head placement are prior; the actual foreign-name case form is supplied. No complete Latin-name declension is introduced.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: gefēran ealle = all the companions. ealle is strong masculine nominative plural agreeing with gefēran; the all-quantifier construction remains supplied.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Prior recognition of ealle is not new productive quantifier mastery.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: forwurdon tō dēaðe = perished to death, naturally all died/perished. dēaðe is masculine dative singular; tō states the endpoint/result, not an infinitive marker or the previously supplied function-for sense.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Supply this tō phrase whole; no general goal/result construction is assumed.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: Apollonius āna = Apollonius alone. āna is weak masculine nominative singular of ān in its alone sense, agreeing with the sole survivor; it is not cardinal one or the homographic feminine plural reference form.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: New sense and weak form are supplied only; Unit3 productive cardinal ān does not cover them.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: becōm mid sunde = came/arrived by swimming. sund is a neuter noun; sunde is dative singular after mid. This means phrase is not an infinitive or newly productive instrumental construction.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Supply actual mid sunde; do not infer a productive swimming verb or general mid syntax.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: tō Pentapolim ðǣm Cyreniscan lande = to Pentapolis, the Cyrenian land. The foreign place name occupies the destination position; the native appositional phrase is neuter dative singular, with weak Cyreniscan. Preserve the foreign -im spelling rather than treating it as a native OE accusative-governance rule.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Exact destination/apposition is supplied. No general foreign-name declension or productive tō-goal syntax.

all_actual_feature_boundaries.description: and ðǣr ūpēode on ðǣm strande = and there he came/went up onto the shore. Apollonius remains the understood subject. ūpēode is the actual anomalous preterite of ūpgān; strande is masculine dative singular in the printed local on phrase.
all_actual_feature_boundaries.scope_note: Supply ūpēode and ðǣr; preserve dative strande and do not replace it with accusative from a modern English motion gloss.

FB-I-CREATION-FIRST-DAY-01.source_text: On anginne gescēop God heofonan and eorðan. Sēo eorðe sōðlice wæs īdel and ǣmtig; and ðīestru wǣron ofer ðǣre nēowolnesse brādnesse; and Godes gāst wæs gefęred ofer wæteru. God cwæð ðā, “Geweorðe lēoht”; and lēoht wearð geworht. God geseah ðā ðæt hit gōd wæs; and hē gedǣlde ðæt lēoht fram ðǣm ðīestrum. And hēt ðæt lēoht Dæg, and ðā ðīestru Niht. Ðā wæs geworden ǣfen and morgen ān dæg.

FB-I-CREATION-SABBATH-01.source_text: Eornostlice ðā wǣron fullfręmede heofonas and eorðe and eall hiera frætwung. And God ðā gefylde on ðone seofoðan dæg his weorc ðe hē geworhte, and hē geręste hine on ðone seofoðan dæg fram eallum ðǣm weorce ðe hē gefręmede. And God geblētsode ðone seofoðan dæg and hine gehālgode, for-ðon-ðe hē on ðone dæg geswāc his weorces ðe hē gescēop tō wyrceanne.

FB-I-CREATION-FOURTH-DAY-01.source_text: God cwæð ðā sōðlice, “Bēon nū lēoht on ðǣre heofonan fæstnesse, and tōdǣlen dæg and niht, and bēon tō tācnum, and tō tīdum, and tō dagum, and tō gēarum. And hīe scīnen on ðǣre heofonan fæstnesse, and ālīehten ðā eorðan”; hit wæs ðā swā geworden. And God geworhte twā miclu lēoht: ðæt māre lēoht tō ðæs dæges līehtinge, and ðæt lǣsse lēoht tō ðǣre niht līehtinge; and steorran hē geworhte. And gesętte hīe on ðǣre heofonan, ðæt hīe scinen ofer eorðan, and gīemden ðæs dæges and ðǣre niht, and tōdǣlden lēoht and ðīestru; God geseah ðā ðæt hit gōd wæs. And wæs geworden ǣfen and męrgen se fēorða dæg.

FB-XII-APOLLONIUS-STORM-SHORE-01.source_text: Ðǣr-tō-ēacan cōmon ēastnorðerne windas, and se angrīslica sūðwesterna wind him ongēan stōd, and ðæt scip eall tōbærst on ðisse ęgeslican hrēohnesse. Apollonius gefēran ealle forwurdon tō dēaðe, and Apollonius āna becōm mid sunde tō Pentapolim ðǣm Cyreniscan lande, and ðǣr ūpēode on ðǣm strande.

existing_reader_dispositions.reason: Continued deferral; passive/optative demands remain untaught.

unit05_prerequisite_findings.finding: gescieppan-pret-3-sg and sense gescieppan-1 are only supplied; teach whole selected indicative system and its ordinary create+accusative use.

geseon-pret-3-sg and geseon-1 are only supplied. Teach full system, including present first singular and preterite plural, and ordinary see+accusative. Supplied content clauses remain separately supplied.

eall-all and the complete strong paradigm have recognition-only milestones. The all+demonstrative+noun construction is not prior production. Exact local support eall ðā ðing is the provisional design choice; selected neuter plural eall has no -e. Any deliberate promotion must be separately recorded.
geswican has only supplied preterite geswāc and supplied cessation-genitive construction. Full new productive finite system plus geswīcan+genitive must precede independent translation.

flēogan and swimman are absent; scīnan has only supplied optative forms/sense. Add all three full finite systems, with intransitive fly/shine/swim uses; this is new lexical consolidation of I–III, not prior vocabulary.
weaxan is absent; teach full VII system and intransitive plant/tree growth sense.
Required gewyrcean, gefyllan, geblētsian finite systems and ordinary objects are prior productive; weak paradigms must not be relabelled new strong teaching.
This exact span is already assigned in Unit1. Unit5 records an explicit revisit with new tasks and promotions; it creates no duplicate first assignment and does not modify the old contract.

boundaries_to_preserve: Personal first/second genitives stay recognition citations; agreeing possessive adjective lemmas carry the distinct productive morphology.
Reference instrumentals, plural cardinal ān, source āna alone and *sǣwa remain in their recorded scopes.
The productive ordinary weorðan-become sense and its taught wearð form do not promote passive weorthan-1 or wearð geworht.
Source wishes, relative/content/purpose clauses, passive/resultative formulae, inflected infinitives, foreign names and source prepositional constructions remain supplied unless deliberately taught.
Nonfinite principal parts remain supplied citation entries; labelling them and inflecting finite stems does not teach infinitive or participial syntax.
No automatic prefix meaning or additional argument/government rule follows from a finite paradigm.
All future vocabulary/task requirements will resolve against exact form, sense and feature IDs with prior actual milestones retained.
